differences.what: street fence: the engraving draws close-boarded fence on the street line running on north from 1620's corner (x 786 px) to the vignette's edge (about x 1030 px), its top at y 597-600 px and its foot at 652-658 px; the build had no fence on this lot. Built so by T-2455 as a 1.5 m close-boarded run on the street line from the south lot line: on the 50% overlay its south end lands at x 787 px, its top at y 597-598 px and its foot at y 655-660 px, on the drawn boards, and it runs unbroken to the walk gate's south pier at about x 1035 px, just past the drawn boards' ragged end
walk gate: the build's pair of iron leaves between stone piers on the door's centre stands at x 1035-1110 px, past the vignette's edge, where the plate draws nothing; the K11 kit's, reconstructed

the house: the build's front shows from x 961 px (its south wall) to the frame's edge, where the plate draws a tree's branches against the sky and, further off, the frame building beyond 1620's yard. The plate is of May 1874 and the record is of 1904, when the 1911 sheet's '2½B' brick house stands here; whether that house postdates the boards or the engraver left it out the plate cannot say, so the house is not taken down to the plate. A picture of 1616 after 1874 settles it
the walk and the gate: 1616's walk gate and the ground inside its boards are past the plate's edge
differences.how: T-3221: a flagged walk laid from the stoop's foot through the boards' walk gate, whose leaves are now drawn open as 1612's and 1620's are, to the public walk; a stated reconstruction on 1612's photograph (L-k14-walks-1600-block-3215). The plate's boards on the street line, which it does draw, are unchanged

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153).
